Hultman identifies mæni ‘called’ as seemingly a form of mæn- ‘say’. Propose a local derived naming/adnominal form. Its precise morphological category is left open, and the proposal does not independently strengthen the provisional deeper mantrayate etymology of the base.

The gāḍi vehicle-word is most plausibly a regional loan of the widespread gāṛī/gāḍī cart/car word. This is the same deep family as already-linked Kalkoti gāṛi, but direct ancient inheritance of this modern transport term is not asserted.

Propose a regional khilaunā-type loan in the khill/khēl play family, anchored to the *khill subsection that includes Prakrit khillaṇa 'toy'. Notes: Identify rupē as the regional rupee currency word, ultimately in the rūpya/rūpiya silver family. This is a loan-family anchor, not direct inheritance of the money sense from the Sanskrit adjective. The currency sense is supported by Hultman's amount-of-money example.

Compare Gawri sō/sūo, Torwali sōw and Ashkun sew/sawak under sarva. These favor sarva for suvā over the lab's higher-ranked sāra. The exact vowel development and possibility of contact mediation remain open.

Hultman table 25 explicitly pairs perfective vāt with vūn 'come down' and verbal noun vāl. Extend the previously approved verb family to its irregular perfective. The link is through the modern paradigm; it is not a proposal that vāt is an independently inherited vāta or an ancient participle.

Compare Palula trūĩde, Dameli truida and Gawri λīd, all explicitly discussed by Turner as tṛtīya combined with a day-word. Propose trīdē as the corresponding extended formation. Use derived, not direct inheritance of the entire adverb from the bare ordinal; the age of composition and the day-member's exact preform remain open.

Propose ælugān as an inflected regional ālu/ālug- potato loan. Turner gives the ālu/āluka edible-root family and its potato sense in regional languages. Hultman explicitly questions the potato-plural gloss; retain that uncertainty, and leave the g-bearing stem and plural segmentation provisional.

Hultman explicitly analyzes ma=ṭæ, with the retroflex dative allomorph after first- and second-person singular pronouns. Propose a local derived case-marked form from ma; the marker's deeper origin is not assigned. Include Liljegren's maṭē, preserving the source vowel difference.

Parallel local case-marked formation tu=ṭæ, explicitly analyzed by Hultman. Link to the accepted Kalkoti tu base as derived; do not misidentify this modern construction as an inherited Old Indo-Aryan dative tubhyam.

Compare Gawri phut 'fly', phit 'mosquito', and Palula phutto/phutti in Turner. Kalkoti phit belongs to this insect family. Preserve the source's fly gloss rather than silently changing it to mosquito; the masculine/feminine distribution is not identical across the languages.

Notes: Propose a local temporal formation from rāt 'night', plausibly involving the goal/dative marker =thæ and consonant coalescence. The lexical association with night is more secure than this exact segmentation. Hultman's example translates rāthæ as tomorrow but does not provide this etymology; label it as a new tentative analysis, not the source author's claim.

Compare Gawri lúmeṇḍ 'stick', explicitly assigned by Turner to *drumadaṇḍa 'wooden pole'. Kalkoti lumēḍ is particularly close. Include inflected lumāṭum provisionally as a variant of the same stick lexeme, preserving its vowel and stop transcription and treating -um as local oblique plural morphology. Do not confuse the stick word with the separate lumaṭ tail family. Gawri transmission remains possible.

Compare Gawri ṭȫp 'hat' and the widespread ṭop/ṭopī family under *ṭōppa. Kalkoti ṭip is plausibly the local front-vowel form. The family is stronger than a specific vowel history; inheritance versus regional borrowing remains unresolved.

Propose gænarāṭ as an extended human noun based on gæn 'big', with the familiar big-to-elder semantic development also reflected in Turner's Gawri and Sauji comparanda under ghana. Hultman's example confirms old people and masculine plural agreement but does not analyze the word's internal morphology. The -arāṭ material remains unetymologized; this is a tentative derived link to the base, not inheritance of the whole noun.
